reason: Confirmed in-scope defect (claim c1): kernel.py uses round-up reciprocal magic _MULTIPLIER=2454267027, _SHIFT=34, with 7*M = 2^34 + 5, so (n*M)>>34 equals floor(n/7) only while 5n < 2^34. Runtime probe t8 shows that for legal uint32 inputs 3435973841 and 4294967291 (both >= 3435973837 and ≡6 mod 7), the kernel returns row = floor(n/7)+1 and col wraps to 4294967295 instead of 6, so col_in_range_0_6=false and 7*row+col != index. This directly violates problem.txt's explicit requirement that "EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal, from 0 through 4294967295 inclusive" and that "every col is in [0,6] and 7*row+col equals the original unsigned index in mathematical integers" — the contract explicitly permits reciprocal multiplication only "if it satisfies this exact requirement for every legal unsigned index," which it does not. The alternative typing concern (c2) was cleanly rebutted (4105 small/mid-range values all exact), isolating the defect to the round-up magic limit, not a dtype issue. No test.py/get_inputs narrow the domain, so problem.txt is the operative contract and these values are squarely in scope. Skeptic reviewed the latest evidence and found no new claims.
